Aztec Ranch Industrial District Page 2 
 
 
1.0 INTRODUCTION 
Aztec Land and Cattle Co., L td. (Aztec) is requesting a zone change for 1,533 acres 
from A -General and RU -20 to IND -1 and IND -2. The request includes additional 
performance standards beyond those required within the Navajo County Zoning 
Ordinance to provide appropriate development buffers from adjacent residential uses.  
 
The property consists of two contiguous blocks of land, generally described as portions 
of the  west half of Section 27 in Township 13N Range 19E , Section 25 in Township 
13N Range 19E and Section 30 in Township 13N Range 20E. 
 
2.0 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF REQUEST 
In 2008, Aztec began the process of developing the Aztec Area Plan, and major 
amendment to Navajo County’s Comprehensive Plan, to create a framework for future 
planning and development of its land, now approximately 240,000 acres . In 2010, the 
Aztec Area Plan was adopted unanimously by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, 
and became the official guiding planning document within the N avajo County 
Comprehensive Plan for all of Aztec’s property.  
 
The Aztec Area Plan was created in anticipation of future zoning and development of 
various properties within Aztec’s land holdings , with early phases being anticipated 
adjacent to primary transportation corridor s and areas where access to utilities and 
services are readily available. Since the adoption of the Aztec Area Plan, Aztec has been 
extremely active in responding to several requests for proposals (RFPs) from both in and 
out-of-state employers seeking to relocate existing operations and/or expand their 
businesses into new markets in the Southwestern United States . Aztec has responded to 
RFPs from box and paper producers, a manufacturer of solar cells and panels, and 
various other users with plans to employ hundreds of people. Typically , these 
manufacturers operate on very short time frames with construction projected to 
commence within months of selection  of a site. This has created the need for Aztec to  
proactively obtain industrial zoning for the property  to reduce entitlement and 
development timeframes and meet RFP scheduling requirements. Taking the initiative 
now will make the property more competitive with other properties, many of which are 
located in or closer to urban areas and have the necessary zoning already in place.  
 
The Aztec Area Pla n and the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan both support 
Industrial zoning through the Industrial/Employment and Community Village 
Character Area designations affiliated with the property. This application is the next 
step in the land planning and developme nt process for a portion of the Aztec land 
holdings that has excellent access to transportation infrastructure, has direct access to 
the Apache Railway short -line railroad with interconnection to the BNSF railway in 
Holbrook, has access to required utilities, including water, power , and natural gas, and 
is suitable in size and location for a variety of industrial uses to support the growing 
need for industry and employment within the region.

<!-- page 746 -->
Aztec Ranch Industrial District Page 3 
 
3.0 EXISTING CONDITIONS ANALYSIS AND PROJECT JUSTIFICATION 
 
3.1 Property Location and Description 
The Aztec Ranch Industrial District includes two separate parcels of land immediately 
north of State Route 277 approximately 5 -miles west  of the Town of Snowflake in 
unincorporated Navajo County, Arizona. See Figure 1, Vicinity Map for the location of 
the Aztec Ranch Industrial District. The first parcel (referred to as the western parcel) is 
comprised of approximately 267 acres of land west of Douglas Parkway within the 
western portion of Section 27. The second parcel (referred to as the eastern parcel) is 
comprised of approximately 1,266 acres of land just west of Indian Pottery Road, 
including all of Sections 25 and 30. The properties are more specifically described as 
follows: 
 
Western Parcel 
Approximately 267 acre s, including portions of the west half of Section 27 in 
Township 13N Range 19E, excluding approximately 53 acres in the southeast 
corner.  
 
Eastern Parcel 
Approximately 1,266 acres, including Section 25 in Township 13N Range 19E and 
Section 30 in Township 13N Range 20E. 
 
See Appendix A , Written Legal Description , for a more detailed legal of the 
property.  
 
 
3.2 Existing Land Use, Comprehensive Plan/Area Plan Designation and Zoning 
 
Existing Land Uses on the Property and Surrounding Area 
The property is currently undeveloped land primar ily used for cattle grazing . 
Immediately surrounding the western parcel is  the Sit graves National Forest and the 
former Catalyst Pulp Mill to the west, undeveloped land used for cattle grazin g and 
ranching to the north, the Apache Railway Company headquarters and service yard to 
the east, and a partially developed residential subdivision and vacant land to the south. 
Tucked within this area near the southeast corner is an approximate ly 53-acre 
exception parcel that has been previously subdivided for residential use, with  only a 
few residences are currently located within the subdivision. The remaining lots are 
vacant with no visible improvements to the property other than dirt roads.  
 
The eastern parcel is also currently vacant and used for cattle grazing . Immediately 
surrounding the eastern parcel is undeveloped State of Arizona property to the west, 
undeveloped State of Arizona and private property to the north, a partially developed 
subdivision with scattered single -family homes and industrial uses to the east, and 
scattered residential properties and undeveloped land to the south.  
  
Comprehensive Plan Character Area Designations 
The subject property is within Planning Area D of the Aztec Area Plan. At the time the 
Aztec Area Plan was adopted, Section 25 was owned by Aztec, and is designated as 
Aztec Industrial/Employment District, consistent with this request. The purpose of this 
district is to promote and encourage a wide r ange of large -scale industrial uses, 
including heavy manufacturing, factories, construction yards, production or transfer of

<!-- page 747 -->
Aztec Ranch Industrial District Page 4 
 
goods, research and development, warehousing, distribution, and support retail and 
office uses.  
 
Sections 30 and the portions of S ection 27 affiliated with this request were not yet 
owned by Aztec, and as a result were not included in the Aztec Area Plan. However, 
they are designated within the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan as Community 
Village. The Community Village character are a designation is intended to provide large 
areas with higher density residential development with a mix of related commercial, 
employment, industrial, institutional and recreational uses extending away from 
highway corridors, highway intersections, future major roadways and existing 
communities in a more urban setting.  Industrial zoning is compatible with the 
Community Village character area designation. See 
Figure 2 , Existing Comprehensive 
Plan/Aztec Area Plan Designation Map  for the location of the chara cter area 
designations within and adjacent to the property.  
 
Existing Zoning Designations 
Sections 25 and 27 are currently zoned A -General in accordance with the Navajo 
County Zoning Ordinance. The main purpose of the A -General Zon ing District  is to 
provide for all the unincorporated areas of the County, except land within the 
boundaries of a reservation and outside the authority of Navajo County, not otherwise 
designated for some other specific zone, to be included in the A -General Zone. In other 
words, the A-General Zone is essentially the blanket zoning designation associated with 
a majority of the applicable properties within Navajo County that have not otherwise 
been rezoned. Uses permitted in the A -General Zone include farm and non- farm 
residential uses, farms, recreational, institutional, commercial and industrial uses 
specifically listed in Article 3 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance.  
 
Section 30 is currently zoned RU -20, Rural Zoning District -Twenty (20) Acres per 
Dwelling Unit. The primary purpose of this district is to conserve and protect open land 
uses, foster orderly growth in rural areas, and prevent urban agricultural land use 
conflicts. The purpose of requiring large minimum parcels of not less than twenty acres 
in area is to discourage small lot or residential subdivisions where public facilities such 
as water, sewage disposal, parks and playgrounds, and governmental services such as 
police and fire protection are not available or could not reasonably be made available. 
Uses permitted in this zoning district include both farm and non -farm residential uses, 
farms, and recreational and institutional uses.   
 
See Figure 3, Existing Zoning Map for the location of all existing zoning districts within 
and adjacent to the property.  
 
3.3 Surrounding Developments, Facilities and Services 
As defined above, the primary uses within the general area include the Apache Railway 
Company headquarters and service yard, the f ormer Catalyst Pulp Mill, and scattered 
residential and industrial uses. The Town of Snowflake is located approximately 9-miles 
to the east, and Heber-Overgaard is located approximately 17 miles to the southwest.  
 
State Route 277 is located immediately adjacent and/or within the property, providing 
excellent regional transportation infrastructure directly to and from the property, and 
connecting to various other state highways and regional transportation corridors in the 
vicinity.

<!-- page 748 -->
Aztec Ranch Industrial District Page 5 
 
A high -capacity natural gas line runs parallel to State Highway 277 through the 
property, providing opportunities for access to natural gas within the development.  
 
Various Arizona Public Service (APS) powerlines and the Zeniff S ubstation are located 
within the immediate vicinity of the property, providing opportunities to serve electric 
power to the property.  
 
A major regional water line  with the capacity of up to 9,000 gallons per minute is 
located immediately north of the property  and can provide industrial water to the 
property.  
 
The Apache Railway short line railroad is located within and immediately adjacent to 
the property, connecting from the BNSF main  line in Holbrook to the Catalyst Pulp Mill 
to the northwest, providing opportunities for rail access to the property.  
 
 
3.4. Public Notification Area and Community Outreach 
In order to ensure all applicable surrounding property owners are notified of the 
proposed zone change request, the applicant has voluntarily agreed to expand the 
citizen notification area from 300-feet to 5,280-feet (1 mile) surrounding the property. 
This will ensure that all nearby residents and property owners are made aware of the 
proposed zone change request, and have an opportunity to participate in the public 
process. 
See Figure 4 , Project Notification Area Map  for all properties included in the 
public notification boundary to be included with this zone change request. Appendix B, 
Public Notification List  - 5,280’ Notification Area  includes the list of all property 
owners within the notification area per the Navajo County Assessor website.  
 
As of the date of this application, Aztec has solicited input (either in -person or 
telephonically) from several  nearby residents .  Although the  names and addresses of 
these individuals are confidential, below is a summary of their general comments:

4.0 DESCRIPTION OF REQUEST 
 
4.1 Project Overview and Zoning Request 
The purpose of this request is to seek a zone change from A -General and RU -20 to a 
mix of IND -1 and IND -2 to allow for the development of light and heavy industrial 
uses in accordance with the Navajo County Zoning Code. The IND -1 zoning 
designation is proposed within 660- feet (1/8 mile) of the perimeter of the property 
where immediately adjacent to existing residential uses . This will provide an 
appropriate buffer between the adjacent residential property owners and the heavy 
industrial uses permitted within the IND -2 zoning district. See Figure 5, Proposed 
Zoning Map for the precise location of the proposed IND -1 and IND-2 zoning districts. 
Within the  IND-1 zoning district , this application request  includes additional special 
development standards to increase setbacks and require buffers between the proposed 
light industrial uses and the  adjacent residential properties along the  perimeter of the 
development.   
 
4.2 IND-1 Light Industrial Zoning District 
The IND -1 Light Industrial District is intended to provide for light industrial uses in 
locations which are suitable and appropriate taking into consideration the land used on 
adjacent or nearby properties, highway access, rail service, and the availability of 
public utilities. Principle uses permitted in this district include the manufacture, 
compounding, processing, packaging, or treatment of materials which do not cause or 
produce objectionable effects that would impose hazards to adja cent or nearby 
properties by reason of smoke, soot, dust, radiation, odor, noises, vibrations, heat, glare, 
toxic fumes, or other conditions that would affect adversely the public health, safety, 
and general welfare. See Article 18 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance for a 
complete list of permitted uses and associated development standards.  Section 4.4 of 
this zone change request also includes additional special development standards that 
apply to the IND-1 district.  
 
4.3 IND-2 Heavy Industrial Zoning District 
The IND-2 Heavy Industrial District is intended to provide for heavy industrial uses in 
locations which are suitable and appropriate taking into consideration land uses on 
adjacent or nearby properties, highway  access, rail service , and the availab ility of 
public utilities. Principal uses permitted in this zoning district include industrial uses 
that are not permitted in any other zoning district. See Article 19 of the Navajo County 
Zoning Ordinance for a complete list of permitted uses and associat ed development 
standards.  
 
4.4 IND-1 Special Development Standards 
The below table identifies the special development standards that shall be applied to the 
IND-1 zoning district. These special development standards will provide appropriate 
buffer standards, including additional setbacks, screening, and landscape requirements 
along the perimeter of the property where adjacent to existing residential uses or 
subdivided residential zoning districts.

<!-- page 750 -->
Aztec Ranch Industrial District Page 7 
 
 
 
 
4.5 Aztec Ranch Industrial District Conceptual Development Plan  
The Aztec Ranch Industrial District has been designed to provide a mix of light and 
heavy industrial uses, while maximizing flexibility for a variety of employment and 
industrial users within the overall development. The light industrial uses are located 
adjacent to existing residential properties to ensure an appropriate transitio n between 
nearby residential properties and heavy industrial use rs. All development parcels will 
have direct vehicle and truck access via local access roads connecting to S tate Route 
277. Additionally, the plan was designed to maximize the number of development 
parcels that c ould have rail access, with three  proposed short track spur lines 
connecting various development parcels from the Apache R ailway located immediately 
to the north.  
 
The Conceptual Development Plan graphically illustrates a variety of parcel sizes and 
configurations which can be modified based on a  specific user needs. For example, i f a 
specific user would like a 60-acre parcel with rail access, a parcel can be configured to 
meet those development  needs. The parcel , roadway and rail spur line configuration 
shown on the Conceptual Development Plan is  intended to be conceptual only, and the 
final parcel configuration will be determined on a phased basis as the property 
develops over time. This will provide for maximum flexibility to adapt to user needs as 
the property is built out.

4.6 Circulation and Access (Vehicle and Rail Access)  
Vehicle circulation will include a series of local access roads entering the property from 
State Route 277. While the locations are conceptual, these access roads will provide 
vehicle and truck access to each development parcel within the overall development. 
While three of the four access roads will terminate at a cul- de-sac designed to allow 
large trucks to turn around, the access road located on  the west side of Section 25 will 
continue northwest into Section 23 and beyond, providing vehicular access to 
additional Aztec parcels to be developed in the future.  
 
Rail access will be provided by up to three new rail spurs, two of which may provide a 
dual connection to the existing tracks to the north, and the third within Section 27 may  
connect from the Apache Railway spur tracks that currently exist within Section 27. 
This configuration will provide maximum opportunity for multiple development 
parcels to offer rail access to industrial users that will ultimately connect to the BNSF 
mainline in Holbrook.   
 
4.7 Utilities and Services 
The applicant has received service  letters from several service and utility companies , as 
summarized below. 
 
Arizona Public Service (APS) : APS has  provided a letter dated April 21, 2017  
confirming that the property is within  their service area, and identifying the conditions 
under which APS will extend necessary power lines to serve the property. See Appendix 
C, Service Letter from APS for details.  
 
Little Colorado  Water Conservation District (LCWCD): LCWCD has provided a letter 
dated April 21, 2017 confirming the property is located within their service area, and 
that they have an adequate water supply to serve almost any type of industrial user. See 
Appendix D, Service Letter from LCWCD for details.  
 
UniSource Energy Service (UES) : UES has provided letter dated April 21, 2017 
confirming the property is within their service area and that natural gas service is 
available to the property. See 
Appendix E, Service Letter from UES for details. 
 
Apache Railway Company (ARC) : ARC has provi ded a letter dated April 27, 2017 
confirming that it is willing, able and capable of providing as -needed rail service to the 
property. See Appendix F, Service Letter from ARC for details.  
 
Taylor-Snowflake Fire and Medical (TSF&M): TSF&M has provided a letter dated 
February 17, 2017 confirming that although the property is not in TSF&M’s designated 
response area, TSF&M holds a Certificate of Necessity issued by the Arizona Department 
of Health for this area, and would respond to all fire and emergency medical needs on 
the property. See Appendix G, Service Letter from TSF&M for details.

1.0 INTRODUCTION 
Aztec Land and Cattle Co., Ltd. (Aztec) is requesting a zone change for 1,533 acres 
from A-General and RU-20 to IND-1 and IND-2. The request includes additional 
performance standards beyond those required within the Navajo County Zoning 
Ordinance to provide appropr iate development buffers from adjacent residen tial uses. 
The property consists of two contiguous blocks of land, generally described as portions 
of the west half of Section 2 7 in Township 13N Range 19E, Section 2 5 in Township 
13N Range 19E and Section 30 in Township 13N Range ZOE. 
2.0 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF REQUEST 
In 2008, Aztec began the process of developing the Aztec Area Plan, and major 
amendment to Navajo County's Comprehensive Plan, to create a framework for future 
planning and development of its land, now approximately 240,000 acres. In 2010, the 
Aztec Area Plan was adopted unanimously by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, 
and became the official guiding planning document within the Navajo County 
Comprehensive Plan for all of Aztec's property. 
The Aztec Area Plan was crea ted in anticipation of future zoning and development of 
various properties within Aztec's land holdings, with early phases being anticipated 
adjacent to primary transportation corridors and areas where access to utilities and 
services are readily available. Since the adoption of the Aztec Area Plan, Aztec has been 
extreme ly active in responding to several requests for proposals (RFPs) from both in and 
out-of-state employers seeking to relocate existing operations and/or expand their 
businesses into new markets in the Southwestern United States. Aztec has responded to 
RFPs from box and paper producers, a manufacturer of solar cells and panels, and 
var ious other users with plans to employ hundreds of people. Typically, these 
manufacturers operate on very short time frames with construction projected to 
commence within months of selection of a site. This has created the need for Aztec to 
proactively obtain indu strial zoning for the property to reduce entitlement and 
development timeframes and meet RFP schedu ling requirements. Taking the initiative 
now will make the property more competit ive with other properties, many of which are 
located in or closer to urban areas and have the necessary zoning already in place. 
The Aztec Area Plan and the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan both support 
Indu strial zoning through the Industrial/Employment and Community Village 
Character Area designations affiliated with the property. This application is the next 
step in the land planning and development process for a portion of the Aztec land 
holdings that has excellent access to transportation infrastructure, has direct access to 
the Apache Railway short-line railroad with interconnection to the BNSF railway in 
Holbrook, has access to required utilities, including water , power, and natura l gas, and 
is suitable in size and location for a variety of industrial uses to support the growing 
need for industry and employment within the region.

3.0 EXISTING CONDil10NS ANALYSIS AND PROJECT JUSTIFICATION 
3.1 Property Location and Description 
The Aztec Ranch Industrial District includes two separate parcels of land immediately 
north of State Route 2 77 approx imately 5-miles west of the Town of Snowflake in 
unincorpo rated Navajo County, Arizona. See Figure 1, Vicinity Map for the location of 
the Aztec Ranch Industrial District. The first parcel (ref erred to as the western parcel) is 
comprised of approximately 267 acres of land west of Douglas Parkway within the 
western portion of Section 27. The second par cel (referred to as the eastern parcel) is 
comprised of approximately 1,266 acres of land just west of Indian Pottery Road, 
including all of Sections 25 and 30. The properties are more specifically described as 
follows: 
Western Parcel 
Approximat ely 267 acres, includin g portions of the west half of Section 27 in 
Township 13N Range 19E, excluding approximately 53 acres in the southeast 
corner. 
Eastern Parcel 
Approximately 1,266 acres, includin g Section 25 in Township 13N Range 19E and 
Section 30 in Township 13N Range ZOE. 
See Appendix A, Written Legal Description, for a more detailed legal of the 
property. 
3.2 Existing Land Use, Comprehensive Plan/ Area Plan Designation and Zoning 
Existing Land Uses on the Property and Surrounding Area 
The property is currently undeveloped land primarily used for cattle grazing. 
Immediately surrounding the western parcel is the Sit.graves National Forest and the 
former Catalyst Pulp Mill to the west, undeve loped land used for cattle grazing and 
ranching to the north , the Apache Railway Company headquarters and service yard to 
the east, and a partially developed residen tial subdivision and vacant land to the south . 
Tucked within this area near the southeas t corner is an approximately 53-acre 
except ion parcel that has been previou sly subdivided for residential use, with only a 
few residences are currently located within the subdivision. The remaining lots are 
vacant with no visible improvements to the property other than dir t roads. 
The eastern parcel is also currently vacant and used for cattle grazing . Immediately 
surrounding the eastern parcel is undeveloped State of Arizona property to the west, 
undeveloped State of Arizona and private property to the north, a partially developed 
subdivision with scattered single-family homes and industria l uses to the east, and 
scattered residential properties and undeveloped land to the south. 
Comprehensive Plan Character Area Designations 
The subject property is within Planning Area D of the Aztec Area Plan. At the time the 
Aztec Area Plan was adopted, Section 25 was owned by Aztec, and is designated as 
Aztec Indu strial/Employment District, consistent with this request. The purpose of this 
district is to promote and encourage a wide range of large-scale industr ial uses, 
includin g heavy manufacturing, factories, construct ion yards, production or transfer of 
Aztec Ranch Indu strial District Page 3

<!-- page 785 -->
goods, research and development, warehousing, distribu tion, and suppor t reta il and 
office uses. 
Sections 30 and the portions of Section 2 7 affiliated with this reques t were not yet 
owned by Aztec, and as a result were not included in the Aztec Area Plan. However, 
they are designated within the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan as Community 
Village. The Community Village character area designation is intended to provide large 
areas with higher density residential development with a mix of related commercial, 
employmen t, indu stria l, institutional and recreational uses extending away from 
highway corridors, highway intersectio ns, future major roadways and existing 
communities in a more urban setting. Indu strial zoning is compatible with the 
Community Village character area designation. See Figure 2, Existing Comprehensive 
Plan/ Aztec Area Plan Designation Map for the location of the character area 
designations within and adjacent to the property. 
Existing Zoning Designations 
Sections 25 and 2 7 are currently zoned A-General in accordance with the Navajo 
County Zoning Ordinance. The main purpose of the A-General Zoning District is to 
provide for all the unincorporated areas of the County, except land within the 
boundaries of a reservation and outside the authority of Navajo County, not otherwise 
designated for some other specific zone, to be included in the A-General Zone. In other 
words, the A-General Zone is essentially the blanket zoning designation associated with 
a majority of the applicable properties within Navajo County that have not otherwise 
been rezoned. Uses permitted in the A-General Zone include farm and non-farm 
residentia l uses, farms, recreational, institutional, commercial and industrial uses 
specifically listed in Article 3 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance. 
Section 30 is currently zoned RU-20, Rural Zoning District-Twenty (20) Acres per 
Dwelling Unit. The primary purpose of this district is to conserve and protect open land 
uses, foster orderly growth in rural areas, and prevent urban agricultural land use 
conflicts. The purpos e of requiring large minimum parc els of not less than twenty acres 
in area is to discourage small lot or residentia l subdivisions where public facilities such 
as water, sewage disposal, parks and playgrounds, and governmental services such as 
police and fire protection are not available or could not reasonably be made available. 
Uses permitted in this zoning district include both farm and non-farm residential uses, 
farms, and recreational and institutional uses. 
See Figure 3, Existing Zoning Map for the location of all existing zoning districts within 
and adjacent to the property. 
3.3 Surrounding Developments , Facilities and Services 
As defined above, the primary uses within the genera l area include the Apache Railway 
Company headquarters and service yard, the former Catalyst Pulp Mill, and scattered 
residential and industrial uses. The Town of Snowflake is located approximately 9-miles 
to the east, and Heber-Overgaard is located approximately 17 miles to the southwest. 
State Route 277 is located immediately adjacent and/or within the property, providing 
excellent regional transportation infrastructure directly to and from the property, and 
connecting to various other state highwa ys and regional transportation corridors in the 
vicin ity.

A high-capacity natural gas line runs parall el to State Highway 277 through the 
property, providing opportunities for access to natural gas within the development. 
Various Arizona Public Service (APS) powerlines and the Zeniff Substation are located 
within the immediat e vicinity of the property, providing opportunities to serve electric 
power to the property. 
A major regional water line with the capacity of up to 9,000 gallons per minute is 
located immediately north of the property and can provide industrial water to the 
property. 
The Apache Railway short line railroad is located with in and immediately adjacent to 
the property, connecting from the BNSF main line in Holbrook to the Catalyst Pulp Mill 
to the northwest, providing opportunities for rail access to the property.

4.0 DESCRIPTION OF REQUEST 
4.1 Project Overview and Zoning Request 
The purpose of this request is to seek a zone change from A-General and RU-20 to a 
mix of IND-1 and IND-2 to allow for the development of light and heavy industr ial 
uses i n accordance with the Navajo County Zoning Code. The IND-1 zoning 
designation is proposed within 660-feet (1/8 mile) of the perimeter of the proper ty 
where immedia tely adjacen t to existing resident ial uses. This will provide an 
appropriate buffer between the adjacent residential property owners and the heavy 
industrial uses permitted within the IND-2 zoning district. See Figure 5, Proposed 
Zomng Map for the precise location of the proposed IND-1 and IND-2 zoning districts. 
Within the IND-1 zoning district , this appl ication request includes additional special 
development standards to increase setbacks and require buffers between the proposed 
light industrial uses and the adjacent reside ntial properties along the perimeter of the 
development. 
4.2 IND-1 Light Industrial Zoning District 
The IND- 1 Light Industrial District is intended to provide for light industrial uses in 
locations which are suitable and appropriate taking into consideration the land used on 
adjacent or nearby properties, highway access, rail service, and the availability of 
public utilities. Principle uses permitted in this district include the manufacture , 
compounding, processing, packaging, or treatment of materials which do not cause or 
produce objectionable effects that would impose haza rds to adjacent or nearby 
properties by reason of smoke, soot, dust, radiation, odor , noises, vibrations, heat, glare, 
toxic fumes, or other conditions that would affect adversely the public health, safety, 
and general welfare. See Article 18 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance for a 
complete list of permitted uses and associated development standards . Section 4.4 of 
this zone change request also includes addit ional special development standards that 
apply to the IND- 1 district. 
4.3 IND-2 Heavy Industrial Zoning District 
The IND-2 Heavy Industrial District is intended to provide for heavy industrial uses in 
locations which are suitable and appropriate taking into consideration land uses on 
adjacent or nearby properties, highway access, rail service, and the availability of 
public utilities. Principal uses permitted in this zoning district include industria l uses 
that are not permitted in any other zoning district. See Article 19 of the Navajo County 
Zoning Ordinanc e for a complete list of permitted uses and associated development 
standa rds. 
4.4 IND-1 Special Development Standards 
The below table identifies the special development standards that shall be applied to the 
IND-1 zoning district. These special development standards will provide appropriate 
buffer standards, including additional setbacks, screening, and landscape requirements 
along the perimeter of the property where adjacent to existing residential uses or 
subdivided residential zoning districts.

4.5 Aztec Ranch Industrial District Conceptual Development Plan 
The Aztec Ranch Industrial District has been designed to provide a mix of light and 
heavy industrial uses, while maximizing flexibility for a variety of employment and 
industrial users within the overall development. The light industrial uses are located 
adjacent to existing residential properties to ensure an appropriat e transition between 
nearby residential properti es and heavy industrial users. All development parce ls will 
have direct vehicle and truck access via local access road s c onnecting to State Route 
277. Additionally, the plan was designed to maximize the number of development 
parcels that could have rail access, with three proposed short track spur lines 
connecting various development parcels from the Apache Railway located immediately 
to the north. 
The Conceptual Development Plan graphically illustrate s a variety of parcel sizes and 
configurations which can be modified based on a specific user needs. For example, if a 
specific u ser would like a 60-acre parcel with rail access, a parcel can be configured to 
meet those development needs. The parcel, roadway and rail spur line configuration 
shown on the Conceptual Development Plan is intended to be conceptua l only, and the 
final parcel configurat ion will be determined on a phased basis as the property 
develops over time. This will provide for maximum flexibility to adapt to user needs as 
the property is built out. 
Aztec Ranch Indu strial District Page 7

4.6 Circulation and Access (Vehicle and Rail Access) 
Vehicle circulation will include a series of local access roads entering the property from 
State Route 277. While the locations are conceptual, these access roads will provide 
vehicle and truck access to each development parcel within the overall developmen t. 
While thr ee of the four access roads will terminate at a cul-de-sac designed to allow 
large trucks to turn around, the access road located on the west side of Section 25 will 
continue northwest into Section 23 and beyond, providing vehicular access to 
addi tional Aztec parcels to be developed in the future. 
Rail access will be provided by up to three new rail spurs, two of which may provide a 
dual connection to the existing tracks to the north, and the third within Section 2 7 may 
connect from the Apache Railway spur tracks that currently exist within Section 27. 
This configuration will provide maximum opportunity for multiple development 
parcels to offer rail access to industrial users that will ultimately connect to the BNSF 
mainline in Holbrook.

Appendix D, Servjce Letter from LCWCD for details. 
Unisource Energy Service (UES): UES has provided letter dated April 21, 2017 
confirming the property is within their service area and that natural gas service is 
available to the property. See Appendix E, Servjce Letter from UESfor details. 
Apache Railway Company (ARC): ARC has provided a letter dated April 27, 2017 
confirming that it is willing, able and capable of providing as-needed rail service to the 
property. See Appendix F, Servjce Letter from ARC for details. 
Taylor-Snowflake Fire and Medical (TSF&M): TSF&M has provided a letter dated 
February 17, 2017 confirmin g that although the property is not in TSF&M's designated 
response area, TSF&M holds a Certificate of Necessity issued by the Arizona Departmen t 
of Health for this area, and would respond to all fire and emergency medical needs on 
the prop erty. See Appendix G, Service Letter from TSF&M for details.

NAVAJO COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT 
PLANNING & ZONING 
 
 
STAFF REPORT  
BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
 
Hearing Date: August 22, 2017 
Case No: 17-20 
Action : Zone Change 
Applicant/Owner:  Aztec Land and Cattle Co. Ldt . 
PARCEL INFORMATION: 
 
Address: 3725 Catalyst Road   
  
APN: 201-01-012, 201-05-007, 
 201-05-001B 
 
Legal Desc:  Township 13 North, Range 19 East, Section 25, 27, and Township 13 
North, Range 20 East, Section 30 in the Clay Springs area. 
 
District: III & IV 
 
Area: Snowflake, AZ 
 
Parcel Size: 1,533 Acres 
 
 
 
STATED REASON FOR REQUEST:  The applicant is requesting a zone change from A-General 
and RU-20 to Light Industrial (Ind-1) and Heavy Industrial (Ind-2) to allow the development of the 
subject property as an industrial district.  The subject parcels are located west of Snowflake, north 
of Highway 277, near the Pulpmill Road intersection. 
 
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD: The surrounding area is a mix of rural 
undeveloped land with some residential homes (RU-5, RU-20, and A-General) with parcels 
varying in size.

<!-- page 822 -->
ZONING DISTRICTS:  
ARTICLE 3 – (A-GENERAL) GENERAL ZONING DISTRICT    
Section 301 - Purpose.  
- The main purpose of this A-General Zone is to provide for all the unincorporated area of the 
County, except land within the boundary of a reservation and outside the authority of Navajo 
County not otherwise designated for some other specific zone, to be included in the "A -General 
Zone", by this Ordinance. No subdividing shall be conducted or approved in the "A -General 
Zone", without prior re -zoning of the land so intended. Uses permitted in the "A -General Zone", 
include farm and non -farm residential uses, farms, recreational, insti tutional, commercial and 
industrial uses as specifically listed in this Article.  
 
ARTICLE 4  - (RU-20) RURAL ZONING DISTRICT   
Section 401 - Purpose.  
- The primary purpose of this district is to conserve and protect open land uses, foster orderly growth 
in ru ral areas, and prevent urban agricultural land use conflicts. The purpose of requiring large 
minimum parcels of not less than twenty (20) acres in area is to discourage small lot or residential 
subdivisions where public facilities such as water, sewage dis posal, parks and playgrounds, and 
governmental services such as police and fire protection are not available or could not reasonably 
be made currently available. Uses permitted in this zoning district include both farm and non -farm 
residential uses, farms, and recreational and institutional uses. 
 
ARTICLE 18 - (IND-1) LIGHT INDUSTRIAL ZONING DISTRICT 
Section 1801 - Purpose. 
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for light industrial uses in locations which 
are suitable and appropriate taking into consideration the land uses on adjacent or nearby 
properties, access to a major street or highway, rail service or other means of transportation, and 
the availability of public utilities.  Principle uses permitted in this zoning district include the 
manufacture, compounding, processing, packaging or treatment of materials which do not cause or 
produce objectionable effects that would impose hazards to adjacent or other properties by reason 
of smoke, soot, dust, radiation, odor, noises, vibrations, heat, glare, toxic fumes, or other conditions 
that would affect adversely the public health, safety and general welfare. 
 
ARTICLE 19 - (IND-2) HEAVY INDUSTRIAL ZONING DISTRICT  
Section 1901 - Purpose. 
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for heavy industrial uses in locations which 
are suitable and appropriate taking into consideration land uses on adjacent or nearby properties, 
access to a maj or street or highway, rail service or other means of transportation, and the availability 
of public utilities.  Principal uses permitted in this zoning district include industrial uses that are not 
permitted in any other zoning district. 
 
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The Navajo County Comprehensive Plan, characterizes the area 
as Community Village.  (Section 4.4.4 of the Comprehensive Plan.) 
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
1. The legal notice for this item has been printed in the local  newspaper, in compliance 
with Arizona Revised Statutes and Article 29 of the Zoning Ordinance. 
 
2. The applicant has submitted the supporting documents required by Section 2902 (1), 
and said supporting documents are complete and adequate for the  Board’s 
purposes. 
3. The subject property is currently zoned A-General (General Zoning) and RU-20 
(Rural Zoning District 20 Acres per unit).  
4. The applicant has submitted a narrative titled Aztec Ranch Industrial District, dated 
May 2017 as prepared by LVA Urban Design Studio. 
5. The Planning & Zoning Commission approved this zone change request unanimously

<!-- page 823 -->
at the July 20th public hearing.

PLANNING AND ZONING RECOMMENDATION:  Should the Board of Supervisors approve  
this Zone Change, staff and the Planning and Zoning Commission recommend the following 
conditions be applied (these conditions were provided to the Owner’s representative prior to 
the public hearing): 
 
1.  Perimeter building setback of three-hundred (300) feet in the IND-1 Distri ct and, in IND-2 
District where adjacent to an existing residential use or existing residential zoning district 
(including RU-1, RU-5, and RU-20 Districts). This setback shall apply to all buildings, outdoor 
industrial uses and outdoor industrial storage.  
2. Perimeter building setback of forty (40) feet from the 277 Highway existing easements or right-
of-way where not adjacent to an existing residential use or residential zoning district.  
3.  Interior building setbacks of twenty (20) feet from all interior roadways within the development.  
4.  All outdoor storage, outdoor uses and/or loading dock shall be screened from view with a 
minimum 8-foot tall solid wall or fence where within six-hundred sixty (660) feet and directly 
visible from a residential use or residential zoning district. 
5.  Perimeter landscape setback of thirty (30) feet shall be provided if a perimeter screen wall is 
located near the property line adjoining a residential use or residential zoning zone.  
6.  All lighting on the subject parcels shall be fully shielded to minimize light pollution and light 
trespass. 
7. Future development of the site (new construction) shall comply with all applicable Navajo 
County requirements, including those of the Zoning Ordinance, Flood Control Ordinance, 
Building Safety ordinance, etc.

A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
APPROVING A ZONE CHANGE FOR AZTEC RANCH & CATTLE CO 
 
WHEREAS, an application for a Zone change was duly filed on May 30, 2017   by Aztec Ranch 
& Cattle Co. Ltd. , requesting a Zone C hange from the A -General and RU -20 zoning 
classification to the Industrial 1 and Industrial 2  zoning classification as shown on the exhibit 
labeled Figure 5; and

APN 201-05,007 which is a portion of Section 27; APN 201 -05-001B which is Section 25 of 
T13N, R 19E and APN 202 -01-012 which is a portion of Section 30 in T13N R20E , west of 
Snowflake; and  
 
WHEREAS the application was considered by the Navajo County Planning & Zoning  
Commission at a duly noticed public hearing on July 20, 2017; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors after considering the testimony and other 
evidence presented at the hearing, as well as the recommendations of staff, found that the Zone 
Change, as connected to the Aztec Ranch Industrial District exhibits dated July 20 LVA -0827 
Typical Buffer Exhibit, is consistent with the public health, safety and gener al welfare and 
should be approved subject to the conditions set forth herein; and 
 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT R ESOLVED the Board of Supervisors hereby approves the Zone

district (including RU-1, RU-5, and RU-20 Districts). This setback shall apply to all 
buildings, outdoor industrial uses and outdoor industrial storage.

right-of-way where not adjacent to an existing residential use or residential zoning 
district.

development.

Board of Supervisors Regular 8.c.        
Meeting Date: 08/22/2017  
Title: Revision to the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance to modify the definition of the
term "Garage, Private"
Submitted For: Glenn Kephart, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Sandra Phillips, Assistant County Engineer/Flood Control Manager
Department: Public Works Division: Planning & Zoning
Presented By: Sandra Phillips
Motion before the Board:
PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and adoption of Resolution Number 27-
17 approving/denying a revision to the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance to modify the definition
of the term "Garage, Private". 
Background:
Staff requests a revision to the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance to modify the definition of the
term "Garage, Private". From - "An accessory building or portion of a principal building
designed or used for the parking or temporary storage of motor vehicles of occupants in the
building to which such garage is accessory, but not including the parking or temporary storage of
recreation vehicles, motor homes, delivery or truck motor vehicles having a capacity in excess of
one (1) ton". To:  "A portion of a principal building or a separate building, designed or used for
the parking or storage of motor vehicles of occupants in the building to which such garage is
accessory.  Structure shall be enclosed or screened on all four (4) sides.  Garages shall meet all
setback requirements.".
The current definition has caused confusion with our residents. The proposed modification does
not change the intent but rather is intended to provide additional clarification and is consistent
with the definition used by other counties within the state as shown on the attachment. 
Planning & Zoning Commission unanimously approved this item at the public meeting held on
July 20th.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval of this change of definition of Garage,Private in the Navajo County
Zoning Ordinance.

GARAGES: 
•Openings from a private garage directly into a room used for sleeping shall not be  
permitted. (R302.5) 
•Other openings between the garage and the residence shall be equipped with solid  
wood, not less than 1 3/8 inches thick, solid or honeycomb core steel, not less than 1  
3/8 inches thick or 20 minute fire rated doors. Door shall be self-closing and self 
latching. (R302.5.1) 
•Ducts in the garage and ducts penetrating the walls or ceilings separating the  
dwelling from the garage shall be constructed of a minimum No. 26 gage sheet steel  
or other approved material and shall have no openings into the garage. (R302.5.2) 
•The garage shall be separated from the residence and its attic areas with not less  
than 1/2 inch gypsum board. For all habitable rooms above the garage not less than  
5/8 inch Type “X” gypsum board. Where separation is a floor – ceiling assembly, the 
structural supporting the separation shall also be protected by not less than 1/2 inch  
gypsum board. (Table R302.6) 
•The floor surfaces shall be of approved noncombustible material. (R309.1)

<!-- page 840 -->
•The area of floor used for parking of automobiles or other vehicles shall be sloped to 
facilitate the movement of liquids to a drain or toward the main vehicle entry  
doorway. (R309.1) 
•Termite pre-treatment required if attached to habitable space. (R318) 
•Private garages classified as Group U occupancies shall not exceed 1,000 square feet 
in area or one story in height except as provided in section 406.1.2 of the  
International Building Code. (IBC 406.1.1) 
•Group U occupancies used for the storage of private or pleasure-type motor vehicles 
where no repair work is done or fuel dispensed are permitted to be 3,000 square  
feet when the provisions of the International Building Code section 406.1.2 are met.  
(IBC 406.1.2)

Currently in the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance: 
 
34. Garage, Private:   
 
 An accessory building or portion of a principal building designed or used for the 
parking or temporary storage of motor vehicles of occupants in the building to 
which such garage is accessory, but not including the parking or temporary 
storage of recreation vehicles, motor homes, delivery or truck motor vehicles 
having a capacity in excess of one (1) ton.   
 
35. Garage, Public:   
 
A building or portion thereof, other than a private garage, designed or used for 
servicing, repairing, equipping, hiring, selling, or storing motor vehicles. 
 
 
Suggested wording: 
 
Garage, Private: 
A portion of a principal building or a separate building, designed or used for the 
parking or storage of motor vehicles of occupants in the building to  which such 
garage is accessory .  Structure shall be enclosed  or screened on all four (4) 
sides.  Garages shall meet all setback requirements.

RESOLUTION ____-17 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
APPROVING REVISED DEFINITION OF GARAGE, PRIVATE IN THE NAVAJO 
COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE 
 
WHEREAS, a submittal for the revision of the definition of garage, private in the Navajo 
County Zoning Ordinance was presented before the Planning and Zoning Commission on July 
20, 2017; and 
 
WHEREAS the application was considered by the Navajo County Planning & Zoning 
Commission at a duly noticed public hearing on July 4, 2017; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors after considering the testimony and other 
evidence presented at the hearing, as well as the recommendations of staff, found that the 
Revised Definition, is consistent with the public health, safety and gener al welfare and should be 
approved subject to the conditions set forth herein; and 
 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED the Board of Supervisors hereby approves the new 
definition:  
 
- Garage, Private:  A portion of a principal building or a separate building, designed or 
used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles of occupants in the building to which 
such garage is accessory.  Structure shall be enclosed or screened on all four (4) sides.  
Garages shall meet all setback requirements.
